header: This decides how the "SQL the model wrote" panel LOOKS. The model sometimes writes a long single line, so I lay it out, one clause to a line, for reading: SELECT ticket_no, name, department_code, department, checkup_date, circular FROM nlq.health_checkups WHERE ticket_no = '228757' AND schedule_year = 2026 ORDER BY checkup_date DISPLAY ONLY: I never touch the SQL that is run, logged and stored. A text that already has line breaks (the model laid it out itself) is left as it is. I never split text inside quotes, or anything inside brackets (a function's arguments, a sub-query).

symbols.sig: function keywordAt(sql: string, i: number, words: string[]): string | null

behaviours: the single line from the 12 Oct screenshot is laid out one clause per line, the conditions indented
the layout never changes the SQL: the same words in the same order
SQL the model already laid out is left exactly as it is
laying out twice gives the same as once
empty text is returned as it is
keywords INSIDE quotes are never split
a doubled quote inside a string ('it''s') does not end the string early
a sub-query in brackets stays on its line; only the outer clauses are split
the AND of a BETWEEN is part of it and is not split off
OR in the WHERE gets its own line; the function calls are left whole
JOIN, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY and LIMIT each start a line
a column whose name merely CONTAINS a keyword is not split (ORDERED_BY, from_date, android)
lower-case keywords are recognised too (the text keeps the case it had)
a WITH query: its brackets stay whole
